clue.text: List in which female belfry resident precedes some dead armadillo

definitions.text: List in which female belfry resident precedes some dead armadillo

parts.words: List in which female belfry resident precedes some dead armadillo
parts.note: a female is SHE and a belfry resident a BAT, giving Shevat, a Jewish month; 'some dead armadillo' holds ADAR, the month that follows it, so the list is the Jewish year's months

explanation.surface: A zoological list in which a female bat comes before a dead armadillo.
explanation.walkthrough: Hints of wordplay build two month names rather than the answer: SHE + BAT gives Shevat, and ADAR is tucked inside 'dead armadillo'. Shevat is followed by Adar in the Jewish year.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a list of months, and this one is the Jewish religious year with Shevat followed by Adar.

clue.text: New MP had seat with PM somewhere in north London

indicators.note: joins the two parts side by side, the second following the first
something new is made afresh, so these letters are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Edward Heath was the British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A newly elected MP has taken a seat alongside the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' shuffles MP HAD SEAT into HAMPSTEAD; Edward Heath was a Conservative Prime Minister (1970-74).
explanation.definitionFit: It is the large open parkland of north London, a place in the city's north.

clue.text: Kind of shorts covering figure's expanse in Caribbean

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece covering another sits above it

parts.note: Bermudas are knee-length shorts
a triangle is a geometric figure; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Some style of shorts conceals a person's figure while on a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like someone's body, but it is a shape in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious zone of ocean between Bermuda, Florida and Puerto Rico, touching the Caribbean region, is a stretch of sea.

clue.text: City house getting call back

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A firm in a city office receives a returned telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound bouncing off a surface returns the shout, a call coming back to the caller.

clue.text: Dog tailed miner

indicators.note: to tail something is to cut its tail off, so the last letter of the word for miner goes

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A dog followed a mine worker around.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish sheepdog breed, such as the Border breed used for herding, is a type of dog.

clue.text: Pay attention and 'elp units out

indicators.note: out describes letters knocked out of place, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch plea for attention: 'Help, units are out!'
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'elp leaves exactly the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperative telling someone to heed carefully, used as a phrase meaning attend now.

clue.text: Felled tree on path just below the summit

indicators.note: a felled tree is knocked down, suggesting these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A tree has fallen across a mountain path just short of the peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning close to the highest point, a position slightly under the peak.

clue.text: A musical call to arms

definitions.meaning: the 1946 Irving Berlin stage show about sharpshooter Annie Oakley
read literally, an instruction to a woman to pick up her weapon

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the title of a Berlin stage show and, taken literally, an order to fetch a firearm.

clue.text: I know the 2, 4, 6 but how likely is that?

definitions.meaning: 2, 4 and 6 are the even numbers, so the speaker asks after the odd ones, 1, 3 and 5
an idiomatic question asking about the chance of something happening

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a cryptic reading: someone who knows the evens is asking for the odd numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation querying probability, as when a bookmaker's prices express the chance of an event.

clue.text: Usher contracted former West Indian fast bowler

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so a letter is dropped from the cricketer's name

parts.note: Malcolm Marshall was a great West Indies fast bowler of the 1980s

explanation.surface: A doorman had once been signed up to play cricket as a West Indies paceman.
explanation.walkthrough: Malcolm Marshall (cricket) loses one L. 'contracted' looks like 'hired on contract' but means 'shortened'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name an official who conducts people to their places at a ceremony; as verbs, both mean to guide.

clue.text: Stay / solid

definitions.meaning: to stem or stop a flow, especially of blood, a verb sense
firm and loyal, as a dependable supporter is

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stop a flow such as bleeding; as an adjective it means steadfast and loyal.

clue.text: Small university publisher and developer

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A minor academic press also develops new authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developer' is the photographer's chemical bath, nicknamed this in darkroom slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkroom slang names the photographic developing solution after a broth, a crossword-favoured sense.

clue.text: Way sportsmen will get free entertainment, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is said aloud and then written as a sound-alike

parts.note: sportsmen are SIDES (teams) and free entertainment is a TREAT, so the phrase says 'sides treat'

explanation.surface: Teams of sportsmen are promised some complimentary hospitality.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor road branching off a main one is a route, so it is a way in the sense of a thoroughfare.

clue.text: Infernal woman, by herself on the blower

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself, in itself
the blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A woman from hell sits alone, chatting on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the blower' is British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was carried off by Hades to be queen of the underworld, so she is a woman of hell.

clue.text: Hyped up, having told Republican to go away

indicators.note: the Republican is made to go away, removed from the word for told

parts.note: to relate a story is to tell it

explanation.surface: An excited person has ordered a Republican to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe being in high spirits and thrilled, synonyms for excited.

clue.text: Driver and drug-smuggler on the level, we're told

indicators.note: joins the pieces, the second following the first

parts.note: a mule is someone who carries drugs across a border

indicators.note: signals a word said aloud and written as a sound-alike

parts.note: a tier is a level, as in a tiered cake

explanation.surface: A driver and a drug-runner say they are being honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the level' looks like 'honest', but here it is ON plus a level.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drives pack animals, such as a man leading laden mules, is a kind of driver.

clue.text: Rubbish, island being sent up by poet's First Voice?

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

explanation.surface: A poet's lead voice is mocked as rubbish on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dylan Thomas's Under Milk Wood, the First Voice tells the story. 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Voice in the poet's radio play is the storyteller who guides the listener through the piece.

clue.text: Film star's beginning to dance 10 yards off

indicators.note: the beginning of dance is its opening letter
off suggests letters that are out of order, signalling an anagram

parts.note: written as digits, 10 looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A film star starts a dance routine ten yards away.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across but is just the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a Hollywood actress and singer of the 1950s, a celebrated screen name.

clue.text: Tony involved with Egypt's borders? Up to now, no!

indicators.note: joins the two pieces, the second following the first
involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tony, asked if he's been to Egypt's frontier, says no, not so far.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase saying something has still not happened at this point in time.

clue.text: Incite mad purist

indicators.note: mad suggests wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Provoke a fanatical stickler for correctness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to provoke or rouse people into action, phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: State has to work without leaders — that's enough to make you mad

indicators.note: each word loses its leader, its first letter

parts.note: Texas is a US state
operate means to work, function

explanation.surface: A state needs to function on its own, which is maddening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leaders' takes the first letter off both TEXAS and OPERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to irritate someone intensely, to annoy beyond patience.

clue.text: Parisian clergyman's healing powers?

definitions.meaning: a French parish priest, spelt with an accent in French
a remedy, something that restores health

explanation.definitionFit: A French parish priest is so named, and without the accent the word means a remedy that heals.

clue.text: She's from the centre of Youghal, Eire

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

parts.note: IRL is the international code for Ireland

explanation.surface: A woman comes from the middle of Youghal, a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Youghal is a town in County Cork, Ireland. 'Eire' gives IRL, the Irish vehicle code.
explanation.definitionFit: A young female, referred to by the pronoun for a woman.

clue.text: Vessel perfectly captures posh Britain

indicators.note: one piece captures another by holding it inside

parts.note: to a T means perfectly, exactly
U means upper class, posh
GB is Great Britain

explanation.surface: A ship is perfectly taken over by upper-class Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful boat that tows ships is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Gorad, cryptically, or Pluvius

parts.note: the made-up word is the letters RA set inside the word GOD, so it shows the sun god within a deity

explanation.surface: A puzzle word is explained as the Roman Jupiter Pluvius.
explanation.walkthrough: Jupiter Pluvius is the Roman sky god as bringer of showers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluvius, from the Latin for showery, is the title of Jupiter as a deity of wet weather.

clue.text: Our punishment they transmit from on high

parts.note: the puzzle appears in the Daily Telegraph, so our newspaper
lines are a school punishment of writing out sentences

explanation.surface: Our punishment is a heavenly broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' is the newspaper printing the puzzle. Lines are a British school punishment of writing a sentence out many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead wires on poles carry messages, so they send signals from a height.
